marchantites.observations: Fig3 A-H fossil panels show narrow forked straps and terminal flattened rounded depressions; I-K are living comparison only. Fig6 A/B fossil cup has a low rim, unlike the deeper living cup D/E. No gemma bodies will be asserted. Original paper text gives width1.1–2.3mm, length up to18mm, cup1.1–2.5mm; branch angles31–70degrees. Low two-row ventral scales documented; microscopic rhizoids omitted.

winfrenatia.observations: Taylor/Hass/Kerp1997 original micrographs1–8 show layered foundation and cavities with raised separating walls, not a mushroom or freestanding cups. Figures9–16 are microscopic detail and will not become fake visible cells. Source pits0.3–0.8mm wide,0.5–1mm deep, mat1–2mm. A small close-up patch, not entire10cm thallus, preserves pit dimensions. Review title verified: Genomic and fossil windows into the secret lives of the most ancient fungi (2020); mutualism not established.

macginitiea.observations: Original1986 title/date verified on p200. Fossil Fig1–4 and schematic Fig5A distinguish angustiloba by long narrow5–7lobes (range5–9), narrow basal angles and deep sinuses; B–G comparisons are not target. Lamina15–35cm long and12–34cm wide; petioles3–6cm. Associated heads shown on separate axes Fig20–25, mature heads10–15mm. Whole crown proportions are artistic and associations do not imply intact preserved tree.

protospongia.observations: Actual ROM thumbnail pixels viewed, only200x100 resolution; USNM66502 shows rectangular lattice fragment, ROM43826 isolated cruciform rays. Neither is a complete outline. Primary museum description says Burgess body/max size unknown, only fragments; globular/conical outline from other localities and six spicule orders. Planned candidate is bounded curved wall fragment with orthogonal stauract hierarchy; not copied pixels or complete Burgess animal. A modest support slab and assumed slight curvature will be identified as presentation/reconstruction choices.
